races.name: Winning Experience With Moulton Racing Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Pierian
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with 14-day gap, benefits from Marquand's tactical nous and Haggas' 19% strike rate, faces easier company than recent Wetherby effort
runners_data.comment: Finished well when winning at Salisbury and she looks useful; should be hard to beat
runners_data.spotlight: Dam 1m2f-1m4f winner (including Irish Oaks); made a promising start when a close second at Wetherby (1m2f, good to firm) last month and she built on that when finishing well to win at Salisbury (1m2f, good) two weeks ago; looks a useful prospect and she has lots in hand on the figures over her sole rival.

runners_data.name: Spirit Dreamer
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse needing pace to aim at, Watson riding for in-form Balding yard, struggled at higher levels but fresher with only 7-day break
runners_data.comment: Has struggled in two runs this month and handicaps will be more suitable
runners_data.spotlight: Closely related to a 1m4f AW winner but he's struggled at biggish prices at Salisbury (1m4f, good to firm) and Haydock (11.6f, soft) this month; still early days but this is a daunting task and handicaps will be more suitable.

races.paceDynamic: Pierian will set the early pace from her prominent position with no other confirmed front runners in this two-horse novice contest. Spirit Dreamer's hold-up style means he'll track behind and rely on a finishing kick from off the pace. With Pierian able to dictate terms unopposed early, she can control the tempo and kick clear when ready. This race shape strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can capitalize on uncontested leads.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pierian Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Pierian gets an easy lead and dictates moderate fractions
scenarios.body: She can quicken when ready from the front and Spirit Dreamer's finishing kick comes too late. The class difference and tactical advantage proves decisive for the Haggas filly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Spirit Dreamer Late Rally
scenarios.trigger: If Pierian goes too fast early or ties up in the closing stages
scenarios.body: Spirit Dreamer's hold-up style allows him to close strongly when the pace collapses. His Balding stable form and fresher appearance gives him the edge late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pierian Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays steady throughout and no collapse occurs
scenarios.body: Pierian maintains her advantage from pillar to post with Tom Marquand managing the tempo perfectly. Spirit Dreamer never gets close enough to mount a serious challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Close Finish Battle
scenarios.trigger: If both horses hit the front together in the final furlong
scenarios.body: An unlikely scenario given the tactical setup, but if Spirit Dreamer times his run perfectly to join Pierian late. The superior class of Pierian would likely prevail in a driving finish.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Pierian goes off too fast early - could set up Spirit Dreamer's late rally in this small field
Monitor Spirit Dreamer's position turning for home - needs to be within striking distance to use his finishing kick effectively
Observe Pierian's response when Spirit Dreamer makes his move - her class advantage should tell if challenged

races.name: Download The At The Races App Handicap

runners_data.name: Fifty Nifty
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 157 days with solid fast-ground form but faces tactical disadvantage from rear
runners_data.comment: Has had wind surgery and he needs watching in market on return for new yard
runners_data.spotlight: Dual fast-ground winner (1m/7f) for Tom Clover, including on his debut at this track in April 2024; shaped quite well at Kempton (6f, AW) in December but failed to build on that next time and has since left Mick Appleby; has bit to prove after six months off but he's had wind surgery and needs watching in market on stable debut.

runners_data.name: Zubaru
runners_data.note: Progressive hold-up type in good form but headgear trial suggests connections seeking improvement
runners_data.comment: Improver who has won on turf (7f, good to firm) in his last two starts; big player again
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive 4yo who made the breakthrough when forging clear at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) and he followed up under a penalty at Leicester 19 days ago; up another 4lb but he's on a roll and is still relatively lightly raced; big player.

runners_data.name: Berry Clever
runners_data.note: Recent C&D winner who can settle handy enough to avoid worst tactical scenario under penalty
runners_data.comment: Justified favouritism over C&D last week and he's respected under a penalty
runners_data.spotlight: Added to his three AW wins when justifying favouritism over C&D (good) last week; goes back up in grade under a penalty but he was as good as ever last time and he's effective on good to firm; shortlisted.

runners_data.name: Dapper Guest
runners_data.note: Visor first-time may spark revival but poor recent form and long absence are concerns
runners_data.comment: On last winning mark but he's been out of sorts in two runs this season; visor back on
runners_data.spotlight: Defied this mark at Chelmsford (7f, AW) last October but he's been out of sorts at Newmarket and Ascot in his two runs this season; now drops back in grade but he's 1-13 on turf and others are more convincing; reapplied visor replaces cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Jakarta
runners_data.note: Quality hold-up horse returning after 224 days with strong juvenile form but needs things to fall right
runners_data.spotlight: Dual winning juvenile (maiden/nursery) who was off for 324 days before showing mixed form in three starts from September last year, just failing in Newmarket handicap (1m, good) but lesser shows either side of that; it's encouraging that this year's campaign is starting earlier but she comes with risks attached after eight months off; tongue-tie added.

runners_data.name: Stenmark
runners_data.note: Consistent performer switching trainers after 90-day break, effective at this distance but needs pace
runners_data.comment: 7f AW winner; returns for new trainer but has possibilities in first-time cheekpieces
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Southwell (7f, Tapeta) last summer and he posted three solid efforts on AW during the winter; returns for new trainer after three months off but he's effective on turf and seems versatile ground-wise in this sphere; dangerous in first-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Daring Legend
runners_data.note: Struggles on turf recently and hold-up style doesn't suit expected race shape
runners_data.comment: Went very close at Kempton but he's struggled back on turf in last two runs; opposable
runners_data.spotlight: Reappeared for new yard with a near-miss at Kempton (6f, AW) in March but he's struggled at 50-1 back on turf in last two runs; got hampered early on at Ascot last time but he's hard to predict and needs to bounce back near best.

runners_data.name: Drifts Away
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front-runner after 273 days off but won this race last year and faces no pace pressure
runners_data.comment: Four wins last year including in this race; needs a close look back from 273 days off
runners_data.spotlight: Big improver in the first half of last year, with four wins and latest was in this race; struggled in final two runs last season but he remains feasibly treated on his best form and is still lightly raced on turf; needs a close look back from 273 days off.

runners_data.name: Sea Suite
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in good current form with 5lb claimer, well-placed tactically for expected scenario
runners_data.comment: Won on AW in March and he's held his form with three creditable efforts since; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Record of 1-12 but his win came at Southwell (7f, Tapeta) in March and he's held his form with three creditable efforts since; still looks on a workable mark and he's respected in suitable conditions back on turf.

races.paceDynamic: Drifts Away represents the only confirmed front-runner in this field and should enjoy an uncontested lead early on with Sea Suite potentially providing some company from a prominent position. The majority of this field are hold-up horses who will settle behind a modest tempo, creating a bunched field turning for home. With limited early pace pressure, the front-runners and prominent racers gain a significant tactical advantage as the hold-up brigade will need to mount sustained challenges from unpromising positions. This race shape clearly favors horses that can race handy to the pace rather than those relying on closing kicks.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Drifts Away gets soft fractions and stays strong
scenarios.body: The lack of pace pressure allows him to dictate terms throughout and prove hard to peg back. Sea Suite can pick up the pieces if the leader weakens, but prominent racers hold all the aces.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Hero Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and becomes a sprint
scenarios.body: The bunched finish suits a horse with a sharp turn of foot who can exploit traffic problems. Berry Clever's recent C&D win under these conditions makes him the most likely beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Returning Class Tells
scenarios.trigger: If Jakarta or Fifty Nifty produce peak form
scenarios.body: Their higher ability levels shine through despite tactical disadvantages from deep positions. The class gap overcomes positional concerns in what becomes a truly-run race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Drifts Away stops quickly and Sea Suite fades
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace creates carnage in the straight with no clear leader. An unconsidered hold-up horse benefits from the scramble as favorites disappoint.

watchPoints.text: Drifts Away gets away with very soft fractions on the lead and proves impossible to reel in
Berry Clever settles closer than usual which would give him perfect tactical position
Sea Suite's inexperienced jockey manages pace positioning correctly from the gates
Jakarta shows early zip suggesting full fitness return after long absence
Multiple hold-up horses struggle for racing room in expected bunched finish

races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Bincimbal
runners_data.comment: Late-March foal by Too Darn Hot; 325,000gns yearling; sales price/pedigree are positives
runners_data.spotlight: Late-March first foal by Too Darn Hot; 325,000gns yearling; dam 7f 2yo winner (RPR 99), closely related to 1m Group 3 winner Komorebi, half-sister to winners Bright Melody (Group-placed 1m1f/1m2f) and Hawk Power (Listed-placed 1m2f), out of Group 1 Fillies' Mile winner; first juvenile runner of the year for his stable and sales price/pedigree demand a market check.

runners_data.name: Byzantine
runners_data.comment: St Mark's Basilica May foal; 65,000euros yearling, 86,000euros breeze-up 2yo; check market
runners_data.spotlight: St Mark's Basilica May (seventh) foal; 65,000euros yearling, 86,000euros breeze-up 2yo; half-brother to winners Open Secret (1m6f Flat, RPR 81; 2m3f hurdle) and Lone Fighter (7f AW; 72); dam 7.6f 2yo winner (98), half-sister to a useful 1m-1m6f Flat and 2m/2m5f hurdle winner; foaling date and mixed pedigree muddy the water but yard is off the mark with this year's 2yos and the betting should provide plenty of clues.

runners_data.name: Eagle Island
runners_data.comment: By Camelot; January foal; 150,000gns yearling; good family and market check essential
runners_data.spotlight: By Camelot; January (ninth) foal; 150,000gns yearling; half-brother to winners Martlet (1m2f-1m4f including Listed; RPR 110), Stowell (Group-placed 1m4f; 109), Keswick (9.4f/1m2f AW; 87) and Palmerston (1m/8.4f; 86); dam 1m3f winner (90), out of Irish Oaks winner; yard had its first 2yo winner of the year fairly recently; market check essential.

runners_data.name: Shiyam
runners_data.comment: March foal; 200,000gns yearling; fascinating first runner by the brilliant Baaeed
runners_data.spotlight: March (fifth) foal; 200,000gns yearling; half-brother to winners Luther (7f/1m including 2yo Listed/US Grade 2; RPR 115), Good Gracious (Listed-placed 7f AW 2yo/1m turf; 101) and Offer And Receive (1m 2yo/Swedish 7f; 79); dam 7.6f 2yo/1m2f Group 3 winner (101); many an eye will be trained on this first representative as a sire for brilliant racehorse Baaeed so fascinating to see how he goes in the market before showing what he can do.

runners_data.name: Al Hudaiba
runners_data.comment: Won Newmarket novice (6f, good) on debut a fortnight ago; the one to beat under a penalty
runners_data.spotlight: 5-1 and he stabilised a yard wobble when looking green but still coming out on top in six-runner Newmarket novice (6f, good) on his debut a fortnight ago; that form is yet to be tested but the runner-up topped an April breeze-up sale at £880,000 so it will be disappointing if it doesn't work out; the one to aim at under his penalty.

races.name: Norwich Inns Handicap

runners_data.name: Hengest
runners_data.note: Classy hold-up runner with winning momentum but faces tactical disadvantage from the likely slow pace and his reliance on strong gallop
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced 4yo who is 2-2 in handicaps and he's open to more progress; big player
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo; won in good style on handicap debut at Windsor (1m2f, good to firm) 17 days ago and he followed up with an odds-on win at Lingfield (11.6f, good) last week; only 4lb higher under a penalty here and he's open to more progress in middle-distance handicaps; big player.

runners_data.name: Give Me The Night
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who gets ideal pace setup but poor recent form and trainer's 0/5 record in last 14 days raises serious doubts
runners_data.comment: Eight-race maiden and he needs a transformation at this new trip
runners_data.spotlight: Eight-race maiden who has not lived up to his initial promise and he's been well held in five handicaps (7f/1m); now 10lb lower than for his opening mark but he needs a transformation at this new trip.

runners_data.name: Man Of Desert
runners_data.note: Hold-up maiden struggling in handicaps with traffic issues last time, needs everything to fall perfectly to break his duck
runners_data.comment: Ten-race maiden who has form figures of 0487057 in handicaps; others preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Ten-race maiden who has form figures of 0487057 in handicaps; had some traffic issues when prominent in the market at Kempton last week but this is competitive back on turf and he still has stamina to prove at this trip; others preferred.

runners_data.name: King's Hand
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with solid recent form but 10 days since last run and needs pace to develop late to showcase his finishing kick
runners_data.comment: Did well to score after a slow start at Lingfield ten days ago; respected under penalty
runners_data.spotlight: Polytrack winner for Sir Mark Prescott in January; two good runs to start off his time with Joseph Parr and he took a step forward when seeing off seven rivals at Lingfield (1m2f, good) ten days ago; this is tougher under a penalty but he did well to overcome a slow start last time and he's still unexposed on turf; respected.

runners_data.name: Harlington
runners_data.note: Natural front runner returning after 38-day break but gets dream scenario with no pace pressure and proven stamina at this distance
runners_data.comment: Three wins on AW this year but he needs to transfer his progress back to turf
runners_data.spotlight: Six time winner who won three in a row in January/February and he ran another good race when third at Lingfield (1m2f, Polytrack) last month; won on turf last summer but that was off a much lower mark and he needs to transfer his progress back to this sphere.

races.paceDynamic: Harlington is the sole confirmed front runner in this small field and will be allowed to dictate terms without early pressure. Give Me The Night may sit prominent but lacks the natural pace to challenge Harlington early, leaving the leader uncontested through moderate fractions. The three hold-up horses (Hengest, Man Of Desert, King's Hand) will be bunched behind a pedestrian pace, setting up a sprint finish where tactical positioning becomes crucial. This sustainable pace scenario strongly favours the front runner who can control the tempo and kick clear when the hold-up horses are still organising their challenges.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Harlington Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Harlington gets an uncontested lead and maintains his recent form.
scenarios.body: The 5yo can dictate comfortable fractions and has enough tactical speed to repel late challenges, especially with his proven stamina at this trip. The hold-up horses will find themselves with too much ground to make up in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes pedestrian enough for closers to overcome the positioning disadvantage.
scenarios.body: Hengest's class edge and recent winning form could shine through in a bunched finish where his superior acceleration matters most. Man Of Desert and King's Hand would also benefit from this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Give Me The Night can improve dramatically off his lowered mark while tracking Harlington.
scenarios.body: The 4yo could benefit from the pace scenario while sitting in the ideal stalking position, though his poor recent form makes this outcome unlikely. His trainer's poor 14-day record adds further doubt.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Harlington weakens dramatically after 38 days off and Give Me The Night fails to capitalise.
scenarios.body: A messy finish would develop with no clear pace narrative, potentially allowing Man Of Desert to sneak through despite his maiden status. This requires multiple horses to underperform significantly.

watchPoints.text: Harlington's fitness after 38 days off - any early signs of rustiness could completely change the race dynamic
How aggressively Give Me The Night positions early - if he challenges Harlington for the lead it could set up the hold-up horses perfectly
King's Hand's positioning turning for home - his recent form suggests he needs clear running room to deliver his best effort
Man Of Desert's ability to overcome traffic issues that plagued him last week at Kempton
Whether Hengest can overcome the tactical disadvantage of likely needing to come from further back than ideal

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Handicap

runners_data.name: First Folio
runners_data.note: Excellent course record but prominent style threatens to put him in the danger zone behind Twilight Fun
runners_data.comment: Three wins and two places from five C&D starts make him impossible to ignore
runners_data.spotlight: Five visits here have resulted in three wins and two places, all at 6f; made an encouraging return when fourth of nine at Ripon three weeks ago and he's slipped to a dangerous mark; tempting.

runners_data.name: Fantasy Master
runners_data.note: Sharp early speed could help him get best position among the prominent pack but needs to avoid traffic
runners_data.comment: Fine third on return; not sure to confirm places with Neyva's Angel but still a key player
runners_data.spotlight: Wasted little time getting off the mark for this yard when scoring at Chelmsford (AW) in December and it was a fine return when flying out of the stalls before finishing third of 18 at Ascot (again 6f, good to firm; Neyva's Angel fourth) 19 days ago; said to look "absolutely superb" in a recent stable tour and he's a must for the shortlist off the same mark.

runners_data.name: Carbine Harvester
runners_data.note: Prominent runner facing tough draw into congested area with recent wind operation a concern
runners_data.comment: Nothing wrong with this mark but the jury's out after some lesser efforts this year
runners_data.spotlight: Ended 2025 with two good AW runs at Kempton; down the field in three AW starts this year and he had been given a wind op before weakening on his return to turf at Windsor (6f, good to firm) 17 days ago; nothing wrong with this mark and he drops in grade but the jury's out at the moment.

runners_data.name: Valley Ofthe Kings
runners_data.comment: Connections blamed undulations for poor effort latest so this flatter track should help
runners_data.spotlight: Two AW wins last year include one at 6f; didn't run at all badly when midfield in a stronger handicap than this at Doncaster (6f, good to soft) in March but he finished last of nine at Catterick the following month; connections blamed the undulations that day and he'll have no such concerns this time.

runners_data.name: Twilight Fun
runners_data.note: Only confirmed leader gives him tactical advantage but recent form suggests vulnerability in finish
runners_data.comment: Last two runs not good but had excuses; not impossible this C&D winner can stage a revival
runners_data.spotlight: Tends to lead; started the year well on AW but it all went wrong at Newcastle in March and he could only beat one home in seven-runner 5f course handicap a fortnight ago; easy ground probably no help that day and it's not impossible this C&D winner can stage a revival.

runners_data.name: Another Abbot
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suited to race shape with strong recent Ascot effort over shorter trip
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten just over 2l when an encouraging seventh of 17 at Ascot (5f, good to firm) at the start of the month; both of last year's wins came at 6f on a sound surface so has conditions to suit and he's a candidate to step forward.

runners_data.name: Neyva's Angel
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who broke maiden recently and benefits if pace collapses completely
runners_data.comment: One place behind Fantasy Master last time; looked unlucky and could well gain her revenge
runners_data.spotlight: Broke her duck in a Southwell handicap last month then bungled the start before seeing little daylight when fourth of 18 at Ascot (6f, good to firm; Fantasy Master third) 19 days ago; looked to finish that event with a fair bit more to give and she's a key player.

runners_data.name: Style King
runners_data.note: Winless on turf and lacks the class needed from prominent position in this field
runners_data.comment: 0-5 on turf; flopped on AW last time and others hold more pressing claims
runners_data.spotlight: 0-5 on turf; didn't build on his second at Wolverhampton in April when favourite but flopping at Southwell (also 6f, AW) a fortnight later; others hold more pressing claims.

runners_data.name: Travel Agent
runners_data.note: In-form hold-up horse with eyeshield fitted, perfectly positioned for late charge if pace develops
runners_data.comment: Quickly clicked into gear for this yard with eyeshield on; solid second latest; feared
runners_data.spotlight: Quickly clicked into gear for this yard with an eyeshield fitted, scoring twice on AW in April before close second at Lingfield (also 6f, good) last Monday; due for a 1lb nudge in future and he can't be ignored.

runners_data.name: Izzy Fast
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits but 50-1 maiden win suggests this handicap debut may come too soon
runners_data.comment: 50-1 win on her reappearance in C&D maiden but beaten 18l on handicap debut next time
runners_data.spotlight: Made a proper splash when going in at 50-1 on her reappearance in C&D maiden (good; third start) in April but contrasting fortunes when beaten 18l on her handicap debut at Newmarket 12 days ago; that was too bad to be true but does lower expectations somewhat.

races.paceDynamic: Twilight Fun will lead from the gate with no other confirmed front-runners to challenge him early, setting a sustainable gallop. First Folio, Fantasy Master, Carbine Harvester and Valley Of The Kings all want prominent positions, creating congestion and scrimmaging behind the leader from 3f out. This bunching will compromise the prominent brigade and create traffic problems entering the final 2f. The lack of early pace pressure on Twilight Fun combined with the prominent logjam strongly favours either the lone leader or hold-up horses who can find clear water late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Gets Away
scenarios.trigger: If Twilight Fun maintains his kick from the front without serious challenge
scenarios.body: The prominent pack gets tangled up behind him while he dictates terms unchallenged, then kicks clear when the scrimmaging starts. Hold-up horses struggle to make up the ground on the firm surface.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion creates serious traffic problems 2f out
scenarios.body: The pace collapse allows the back markers to sweep through on the outside with clear runs. Travel Agent and Another Abbot benefit most from the change of pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Survivor Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If one prominent runner avoids the traffic and gets first run
scenarios.body: Fantasy Master or First Folio gets the jump on their prominent rivals and has enough left to hold off the closers. The winner comes from those with the best recent form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Twilight Fun stops quickly and the prominent pack implodes
scenarios.body: The moderate early pace becomes a crawl, setting up a cavalry charge from the rear. Neyva's Angel and Izzy Fast get the strongest finish from the back.

watchPoints.text: Twilight Fun's early fractions - if he goes too fast early he'll tie up badly in the final furlong
Traffic problems 2f out when First Folio, Fantasy Master, Carbine Harvester and Valley Of The Kings converge
Travel Agent's position turning in - needs clear room to unleash his recent finishing kick
Another Abbot's stalking position - Marquand must avoid getting trapped behind the prominent wall
Fantasy Master's jump from the stalls - his gate speed could determine whether he avoids or joins the scrum

races.name: Get Raceday Ready Handicap

runners_data.name: Merapi
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with recent course form advantage but faces tactical challenge against lone leader
runners_data.comment: 0-14 but runner-up in last three starts and two of those were at Yarmouth; respected
runners_data.spotlight: 0-14 but she finished runner-up twice here (1m/1m1f) last month and had another close call at Wolverhampton two weeks ago; on same mark as for her last two runs and she should make another bold bid; cheekpieces added.

runners_data.name: Siam Fox
runners_data.note: Hold-up style, long-term course winner but struggling recent form after wind surgery
runners_data.comment: His last win was almost two years ago and he's struggled in last five runs; new headgear
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner but his last success was almost two years ago; very well treated on old form but he's struggled in last five starts including after wind surgery here (1m good; 22-1) two weeks ago; blinkers are now tried and cheekpieces are removed.

runners_data.name: King Of Charm
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 57-day break with disappointing recent efforts
runners_data.comment: On reduced mark but he needs a big turnaround in first-time cheekpieces
runners_data.spotlight: Thrown in on his 3yo form but 2025 was disappointing and he's struggled in both runs this year; mark continues to fall but he needs a needs a big turnaround in first-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: El Fox
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with recent course fourth, needs to overcome positioning disadvantage
runners_data.comment: 0-9 but she's reached the frame in four handicaps including over C&D; in the mix
runners_data.spotlight: 0-9 but she's reached the frame in four of her handicaps including when fourth on C&D reappearance (good) two weeks ago; that was behind a major improver and she's a player if he can build on that.

runners_data.name: Charlatan
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning to turf after AW success, tactical speed question at 1m
runners_data.comment: Five-time AW winner; record of 0-7 on turf but he could be dangerous back in this sphere
runners_data.spotlight: Gained his fifth AW success when winning at Wolverhampton (8.6f) in December; mixed results in four subsequent runs but he rallied for fourth at Southwell (7f, AW) in March; now returns to turf but he has placed form in this sphere and is not ruled out back up in trip.

runners_data.name: Typeface
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with turf wins but disappointed at Doncaster on reappearance
runners_data.comment: Has mixed record since his last win but he's a player if he can rediscover his spark
runners_data.spotlight: Dual turf winner but has mixed record since his emphatic win at Ffos Las (1m, good) last August; didn't live up to market expectations on Doncaster reappearance (good to soft) 12 days ago but he missed the break and may have needed that run; should be sharper this time and has possibilities if he can rediscover his spark.

runners_data.name: Suitcase Smith
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner beaten 6+ lengths recently, hard to fancy despite weight drop
runners_data.comment: Unexposed 4yo but he's not finished closer than 6l to a winner; hard to fancy
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed 4yo but he's not finished closer than 6l to a winner and was a remote seventh over C&D (good) two weeks ago; dropped another 3lb but he's hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Kitty's Dream
runners_data.note: Hold-up style returning after 234 days off for new trainer Ed Dunlop
runners_data.comment: Struggled in six runs for Alice Haynes and has a lot to prove on return for new yard
runners_data.spotlight: Struggled in six runs for Alice Haynes including three handicaps (7f-8.6f); returns for new yard after 234 days off and she has a lot to prove; equipment removed.

runners_data.name: Regal Guest
runners_data.note: Only front runner gets uncontested lead but needs career-best effort to win
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced 4yo but he's beaten only one rival in three handicaps; cheekpieces added
runners_data.spotlight: Promising third at Kempton (7f, AW) last March on his second start but has beaten only one rival in three handicaps since; still lightly raced but he needs a transformation at this new trip; cheekpieces added.

races.paceDynamic: Regal Guest represents the only confirmed front runner in this field of nine hold-up horses, giving him an uncontested lead from the outset. With no pace pressure, he can dictate fractions and control the tempo throughout the 1m journey on good to firm ground. The eight hold-up horses will need to overcome traffic problems and poor positioning as they converge late behind the lone leader. This race shape heavily favours prominent runners who can track Regal Guest early and those with proven tactical speed to secure good positions, while pure hold-up horses face significant disadvantages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Regal Guest maintains steady fractions without early pressure
scenarios.body: The lone pace-setter controls the race from pillar to post while the field of hold-up horses gets bunched up behind him. Late challengers struggle to make meaningful inroads against a horse with first run on them.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Merapi or El Fox secure good early positions behind Regal Guest
scenarios.body: One of the handier hold-up horses tracks the leader closely and has enough tactical speed to strike in the final furlong. The rest of the field gets caught in traffic as expected.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Helps Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the main contenders get shuffled back or blocked in running
scenarios.body: The bunched field creates significant interference problems allowing a 20/1+ shot with a clear run to emerge late. Lesser fancied horses benefit from cleaner passages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Charge Overcomes All
scenarios.trigger: If multiple hold-up horses find clean runs simultaneously in the final two furlongs
scenarios.body: Superior class tells as the better horses overcome the tactical disadvantage through sheer ability. The pace collapse allows them to finish strongly despite poor positioning early.
